overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the chair's statement and apology were outside the committee's jurisdiction, executive session was optional, and veracity questions fell outside the law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the April 26 meeting notice was insufficiently specific because it did not disclose the chair's planned statement and apology about two members.
allegations.key_passage: We find that Chair Alexander’s statement and apology was not a matter within the Committee’s jurisdiction and the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law in this regard.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the two affected members should have received individual notice of the chair's comments about them.
allegations.key_passage: Since Chair Alexander’s comments occurred in open session and not in executive session under Purpose 1, there was no requirement to provide the Caprarellas with individual notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee discussed two members' reputation and character in open session when it should have gone into executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Open Meeting Law allows a public body to enter executive session for one or more of the ten enumerated purposes, it never requires a public body to enter executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint and request for review asserted the veracity and motivations of the chair's comments.
allegations.key_passage: Such matters fall outside the Open Meeting Law, and we therefore decline to review or opine on these matters.

allegations.summary: The request for review implicitly sought review of two earlier complaints filed with the committee on or about May 4.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons outlined in a July 6 letter from our office to Attorney Loew, the May 4 complaints have been closed and we decline to review the allegations raised in those complaints.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
